newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel does not rule out German budget freeze.
newsitem.headline: Waigel does not rule out German budget freeze.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday he did not rule out imposing a freeze on state spending this year to limit state borrowing.
"A freeze is still being discussed and is not off the agenda. But at the moment, there is no decision to impose such a freeze," Waigel told a news conference.

Speculation has mounted that Waigel would have to clamp down on spending to stop record post-war unemployment burdening state finances so much that Germany fails to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Waigel has maintained that Bonn would fulfill the Maastricht Treaty budget deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year so that it can join the planned launch of the European single currency in 1999.
